spec.title: Offered vs accepted (202) vs rejected (503) requests per second
spec.description: Offered = k6_http_reqs_total (all answers k6 saw), accepted = 202, rejected = 503. In an 'over' run the accepted line is the capacity: expect about 1,000 / 455 / 122 req/s at 20 / 50 / 200 ms (pool 25 / (5 ms + latency)). In an 'under' run accepted should equal offered. Surprising: accepted above the prediction (hold time shorter than 5 ms) or below it at 0 ms (proxy is the limit). k6_b3_resp_* are added by this experiment's script.js and exist after the first k6 run. k6 series are not marked stale, the last value can linger after a run.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations (must be 0)
spec.description: k6_dropped_iterations_total rate. In 'over' runs at 20 ms the queue can reach the 3,000 VU cap and drop iterations; that is then a finding to report, not a generator fault. Anywhere else it must be 0.

spec.title: CPU busy % by pinned group
spec.description: Server cores (0,6), Postgres (1,7,2,8), k6 (3,9,4,10), monitoring + Toxiproxy (5,11). Keep k6 under about 70% and the monitoring group (which carries the proxy) under about 80%, else the generator or the proxy is the bottleneck, not the pool. Surprising: cores 5,11 near 100% at level 0 (the proxy is the limit).

spec.title: Event-loop delay and disk busy
spec.description: Event-loop lag (seconds, nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds) and disk busy fraction (node_disk_io_time_seconds_total, 1 = 100%). At level 0 the disk was about 93% busy in B2.

spec.title: k6 failed requests ratio
spec.description: k6_http_req_failed_rate: share of requests that were not 202 (the script counts only 202 as success). 503 in 'over' runs is expected; in 'under' runs it must be 0.

spec.title: API latency seen by k6 (p50 and p99)
spec.description: Native-histogram quantiles of k6_http_req_duration_seconds, split by added latency and phase. In 'under' runs p50 should be about 5 ms + added latency + 1-3 ms (slope 1.0 'one-for-one'). In 'over' runs p50 sits near the 2 s pool timeout. Surprising: a slope clearly different from 1 (two round trips per request, or the latency also hitting connection setup).

spec.title: 503 answers by type (server counter)
spec.description: ep_db_errors_by_type_total. Expect pool_timeout only, and only in 'over' runs (pool wait over 2 s). Surprising: another type (too_many_clients, statement timeout = 5 s) would mean the latency reached something else.

spec.title: Requests in the system: gauge vs Little's Law
spec.description: Blue: http_requests_in_flight (gauge). Second: Little's Law L = arrival rate x mean time = rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum), the seconds of request-time added per second. They should agree (completed requests only, so the second lags during a sudden queue). Expect about 12 in 'under' runs at every level, and up to cap x 2 s (about 2,000 at 20 ms, 250 at 200 ms) in 'over' runs. Surprising: a big gap between the two.

spec.title: Pool: in use, idle, waiting
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_total - ep_pg_pool_idle = connections in use (max 25). waiting = requests queued for a connection. Expect in use well under 25 in 'under' runs, pinned at 25 with waiting in the hundreds or thousands in 'over' runs. Surprising: in use below 25 while waiting is high (connections not being opened, or a handshake stuck on the latency).

spec.title: Query time and pool wait (server side)
spec.description: ep_pg_query_duration_seconds p50 should be about 5 ms + the added latency (this is the hold time H, the divisor in capacity = 25 / H). Pool wait p99 stays near 0 in 'under' runs and reaches about 2 s (the timeout) in 'over' runs. Surprising: query p50 not moving with the level (the toxic is not on the path).

spec.title: Postgres connections by state
spec.description: pg_stat_activity_count from postgres-exporter. With added latency the connections sit 'idle' (the database already answered, the answer is in the proxy), 'active' stays small. Surprising: a high active count at 200 ms (then the database is working, not waiting).

spec.title: Postgres container CPU (cores)
spec.description: rate of ep_pg_container_cpu_seconds_total (from infra/scripts/pg-container-exporter.sh, started by run.sh). Expect it to fall as the level rises, because fewer inserts per second reach it. Empty if the exporter could not start.

spec.title: Commits per second (Postgres)
spec.description: rate of pg_stat_database_xact_commit for the eventpulse database. It should follow the accepted rate and fall in steps with the added latency.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: latency and capacity vs added latency
2. The mechanism: where the time goes (Little's Law, pool)
3. Resource view: is the database the problem? (it should not be)
EventPulse B3 - Slow database propagates to the API
